source_review.notes: Checked all ten final official references on 2026-08-31. Nine URLs returned HTTP 200 and the official EUR-Lex regulation endpoint returned HTTP 202 with the requested authoritative resource available. Verified the Interoperable Europe Act's April 2024 entry into force and co-owned governance/assessment mechanisms, NIST SP 800-63C-4's July 2025 final status, NIST standards page's July 2026 update, and GAO-26-107466's June 2026 bounded findings. EU, NASA, NIST, and GAO material is kept within its stated jurisdiction and subject scope rather than presented as universal law.

evidence: Reviewed six-layer vector I(q,C,t)=<legal/policy, organizational, semantic, technical, operational, assurance>.
Reviewed necessary eligibility conjunction without asserting the converse or compensability among veto layers.
Reviewed bounded claim tuple over outcome, thread, coalition, configuration, environment, thresholds, evidence, exceptions, authority, and validity.
Reviewed partial/lossy semantic mapping notation with domain, codomain, version, preconditions, unmapped values, provenance, and decision limits.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently makes interoperability relational, directional, thread-specific, coalition/configuration-bound, and time-sensitive.

evidence: Executed cross-authority-interoperability-ledger-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-094/report.json.
Confirmed three threads times six layers creates eighteen required checks.
Confirmed seventeen initial passes and benefit_eligibility:legal_policy as the sole missing check.
Confirmed correction yields eighteen declared passes, zero missing, and only metadata-gate eligibility.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as fifteen of eighteen checks, equal to five sixths or approximately 83.33 percent.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts do not validate layer discovery, legal authority, semantics, evidence truth, actual configuration, noncompensable constraints, human work, risk, or outcomes.

evidence: Confirmed connectivity, encryption, successful parsing, or schema conformance does not entail legal, semantic, operational, or assurance interoperability.
Confirmed standard-name equality does not entail compatible version, profile, options, extensions, mappings, or interpretations.
Confirmed convening, advisory guidance, or coordination responsibility does not entail funding, mandate, enforcement, waiver, or risk-acceptance authority.
Confirmed provider conformance and pairwise tests do not entail correct consumer behavior or multilateral coalition outcomes.
Confirmed a signed agreement or certificate does not entail continuing applicability after authority, purpose, configuration, policy, threat, or evidence changes.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Invalid implications are explicitly rejected and conclusions are narrowed to participants, direction, purpose, versions, evidence, and validity period.

evidence: Challenged unlawful but secure exchange, cross-jurisdiction conflicts, classification/privacy purpose, rights/redress, voluntary adoption, unfunded mandates, and absent enforcement.
Challenged identity collisions, code-system editions, local extensions, lossy unknown-to-false mappings, event/effective/receipt time, retroactivity, late corrections, and reference-data drift.
Challenged producer-only evidence, obsolete certificates, local production extensions, gateway transformations, consumer misuse, excluded populations, and misleading admitted-traffic denominators.
Challenged shared-service overload, pairwise/noncompositional behavior, policy denial, emergency overrides, degraded operation, incident response, recovery, appeal, and re-entry.
Reviewed ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, authority mechanisms, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits, affected people, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real decisions require empowered legal/policy and data authorities, participant owners/operators/funders, semantic/domain experts, architects, security/privacy/safety authorities, human-factors expertise, V&V, users, and redress bodies.

evidence: Confirmed each claim names outcome, direction, thread, coalition, configuration, environment, thresholds, authority, evidence, exclusions, and validity.
Confirmed every cross-boundary obligation maps to definition, approval, funding, implementation, operation, verification, veto, waiver, change, and dispute authorities.
Confirmed profiles resolve versions/options/extensions plus identity, concepts, units, time, reference data, provenance, errors, policy, operations, and evidence.
Confirmed effective agreements cover purpose/population, authorized parties, retention/onward use, protection, responsibilities, redress, changes, termination, and precedence.
Confirmed provider, consumer, end-to-end, negative, load, security/privacy, failure/recovery, redress, and outcome evidence is configuration-bound.
Confirmed law, authority, membership, semantics, standards, versions, policies, threats, incidents, dependencies, and operations trigger reassessment.
invariant_checking.notes: No ping, message parse, standard label, committee, gateway, signature, certificate, pairwise test, or aggregate success rate is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem is claimed; the layer conjunction is an explicitly bounded necessary-condition governance model.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled synthetic_interoperability_ledger_consistent and declared_boolean_layer_coverage_only.
Fixture conclusions stop at declared layer-gate eligibility and disclaim evidence truth, real authority, implementation, operation, risk, and outcome proof.
GAO-26-107466 is presented as a bounded federal award/eligibility-data audit finding, not universal evidence about all interoperability programs.
Examples and exercises are synthetic teaching cases, not legal opinions, data-sharing approvals, certifications, operational authorizations, or readiness findings.
Official sources are attributed without claiming EU, NASA, NIST, GAO, or other external review or endorsement.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Source-backed guidance, public audit evidence, internal review, synthetic arithmetic, configured conformance, and competent external authorization remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked relational framing, six coupled layers, authority functions, law/policy, organizational processes, semantics/time, profiles, effective agreements, information protection, consumer duties, standards governance, evolution, gateways, conformance, coalition validation, inclusion, incentives, redress, and interoperability cases.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked profiles, agreements, authority/funding mechanisms, identity/reference data/time, mappings, service processes, security/privacy, producer/consumer tests, gateways, actual effectivity, migrations, incidents, appeals, certification scope, operational monitoring, and retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from outcome and authority through six-layer specification, implementation, evidence, operation, and change. Ten examples and five answers cover alerts, lawful exchange, voluntary standards, code versions, accessible transport, lossy mappings, identity freshness, coalition load, regulatory semantics, certification limits, shelters, coverage arithmetic, data diagnosis, nonmandating governance, and credentials.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external EU, NASA, NIST, GAO, legal/regulatory or data authority, participant owner/operator/funder, semantic/domain expert, architect, security/privacy/safety authority, human-factors specialist, V&V/certification authority, affected user, redress body, auditor, academic, or other practitioner review is claimed.
